title: Coniveau edge and its normalized flag components
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian excellent normal strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, with closed point $s$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $U=S\setminus\{s\}$ and $U^p=\{y\in U:\dim\mathcal O_{S,y}=p\}$. Use ordinary etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], costalks $C_y$, and the normalized immediate transitions and twists of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. There is a convergent cohomological coniveau spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{y\in U^p}H^{p+q}_{\{y\}}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^h_{S,y},\Lambda(d))\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(U,\Lambda(d)).$$
Here $\mathcal O^h_{S,y}$ is the henselization (a henselian local ring universal among henselian local rings receiving a local map from $\mathcal O_{S,y}$), and local supported cohomology identifies with $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y),C_y\Lambda(d))$. Suppose for every $y\in U^p$ the sheaves $\mathcal H^j(C_y\Lambda(p))$ vanish for $j>2p$, and an isomorphism $\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^{2p}(C_y\Lambda(p))$, $1\mapsto e_y$, is specified on the residue-field etale site [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose also that every $\Lambda$-module etale sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ has no cohomology in degrees greater than $d-p$. Then $E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $q>d$ or $p\notin[0,d-1]$, and
$$E_1^{p,d}\cong\bigoplus_{y\in U^p}H^{d-p}(\kappa(y),\Lambda(d-p)).$$
The canonical edge, followed by the localization boundary, gives an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{coker}(E_1^{d-2,d}\xrightarrow{d_1}E_1^{d-1,d})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d)).$$
For $y\in U^{d-1}$ the normalized valuation residue is an isomorphism $\rho_y:H^1(\kappa(y),\Lambda(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$: normalize the reduced closure of $y$ in $S$, take the tame residue of its strictly henselian trait, and divide by the purely inseparable degree of its closed point over $s$. Under the above identification, there is a sign $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, depending only on the sign conventions of the localization boundary, of the residue and of the trait transition (not on $S$, $y$ or $b$), such that the map from this $y$-summand to $H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d))$ is
$$b\longmapsto\epsilon\,\rho_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y}),$$
where the transition is twisted by $d-1$ and $e_{\bar y}$ is the geometric fibre of $e_y$. In particular the image of this summand is $\Lambda\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$.
